title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1968 Avalon show with a smoking Dark Star and stellar Eleven, captured on solid soundboard tape.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its intense improvisations – a beautiful, flowing Dark Star, a fiery Eleven, and an electrifying New Potato > Drums jam that keep the energy high throughout. The recording is a classic 1968 sound‑board source with enough clarity to enjoy the nuances, though a few listeners note slight pitch irregularities.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give five stars and highlight exceptional musical moments; only one notes minor pitch issues. The show is consistently described as high‑energy with standout jams, while the soundboard source is regarded as good quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Classic 1968 sound‑board tape – clear enough to hear individual instruments, with a lo‑fi vintage character. A few comments mention pitch correction needs and occasional abrupt splice, but overall listeners find the recording enjoyable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set strong and cohesive; second set maintains high intensity with seamless transitions except for the jarring cut from New Potato into Drums. Overall pacing is driving and engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise Jerry's masterful guitar work, tone, and soulful soloing, especially on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass playing is highlighted as powerful and tightly locked with the drums, feeding off the group’s energy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers are described as fabulous and fueling the jams; one comment notes the Drums segment was less interesting than earlier parts.
